chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Kowlum, from Abu Saeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When the believer enters his grave, the prayer will be on his right and the alms-tax on his left, and righteousness will overlook him, and patience will withdraw to a side. And when the two angels who oversee his questioning come to him, patience will say to the prayer and the alms-tax: 'You two are beside your companion; if you are unable to help him, then I am beside him.'
ai.seo_question: What role does patience play in the grave for a believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kafi, the personification of deeds illustrates the hierarchical support system in the grave (Barzakh), where prayer and charity act as initial defenders during the questioning by Munkar and Nakir. Scholarly tradition emphasizes that while these acts provide structural support, patience (Sabr) serves as the ultimate, resilient sustainer, remaining with the believer even if other deeds are insufficient, highlighting the centrality of spiritual endurance in Shia eschatology.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Kowlum, from Abu Saeed, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the Believer enters his grave, the Salaat would be on his right, and the Zakat on his left, and the righteous deeds overlooking upon him, and the patience isolates in the corner. And when the two Angels come over to him, the ones who would be questioning him, the patience says to the Salaat and the Zakat: ‘(You two) are besides your companions, so if you are frustrated (from helping him), then I would be besides him’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Mahbub from ’Abd Allah ibn Kulum from abu Sa‘id who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that when a believing person is placed in his grave, his prayer appears on his right side, Zakat (his paying charity) on his left side, his good manners above him and his patience stands on one side. When the angels, who interrogate him, enter his grave, his patience will say to his prayer and Zakat, ‘Help your friend. If you fail, then I will defend him?”
